es.summary: Se creó o modificó una configuración de admission webhook (mutating o validating) en un clúster AKS o Kubernetes conectado con Azure Arc. Puede ser un cambio administrativo legítimo o un mecanismo de persistencia o de robo de credenciales.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de Azure Activity Logs cuyo operationName empieza por MICROSOFT.CONTAINERSERVICE/MANAGEDCLUSTERS/ o MICROSOFT.KUBERNETES/CONNECTEDCLUSTERS/ADMISSIONREGISTRATION.K8S.IO y termina en MUTATINGWEBHOOKCONFIGURATIONS/WRITE o VALIDATINGWEBHOOKCONFIGURATIONS/WRITE.
es.why_it_matters: Un webhook recibe las solicitudes al API server antes de que se apliquen. Uno mutating puede inyectar un contenedor malicioso en cada pod (persistencia) y uno validating puede registrar secrets y tokens (T1552.007, credenciales en la API de contenedores; T1078).
triage_steps: Identifique en el evento el caller (usuario, service principal o managed identity), callerIpAddress, resourceId del clúster y status de la operación.

Obtenga la configuración: kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations/validatingwebhookconfigurations -o yaml. Revise clientConfig (URL externa o service desconocido), rules, namespaceSelector y failurePolicy.
Compare el nombre y el backend con componentes conocidos: cert-manager, Gatekeeper/Azure Policy, Kyverno, Istio, Linkerd. Verifique si hay un release de Helm o despliegue GitOps asociado.
Revise los logs kube-audit del clúster para ver la identidad Kubernetes, el user agent y el contenido exacto del cambio.
Pivotee sobre el mismo caller y clúster +/- 15 minutos: listClusterAdminCredential, asignaciones de roles, creación de pods, deployments o secrets.
Busque alertas anteriores del mismo caller o callerIpAddress y confirme si la IP pertenece a rangos corporativos o de CI/CD.
Valide con el dueño del clúster o con el ticket de cambio si la modificación estaba planificada.
false_positives: Administradores que despliegan o actualizan controladores de admisión de forma planificada.
Instalación o actualización con Helm de operadores como cert-manager, Kyverno o Gatekeeper; cert-manager puede reescribir el caBundle periódicamente.
Add-ons administrados por Azure (Azure Policy, malla de servicios basada en Istio) o pipelines GitOps (Flux, Argo CD).
response_steps: Confirme con el responsable del clúster; si es legítimo, documente y considere una exclusión acotada por caller y nombre de webhook.
Si no está autorizado, exporte el YAML del webhook como evidencia y elimínelo o deshabilítelo tras confirmar que no es crítico para el clúster.
Revise los pods creados desde el cambio en busca de contenedores inyectados y elimine las cargas comprometidas.
Rote secrets, tokens de service account y credenciales que pudieron ser interceptados; revoque o deshabilite las credenciales del caller.
Revise RBAC de Azure y de Kubernetes, limite quién puede escribir admission webhooks y monitoree recurrencias.
es.severity_rationale: Nivel medio: los cambios de webhooks son comunes en la administración normal, pero un webhook malicioso otorga persistencia y acceso a credenciales en todo el clúster.

en.summary: A mutating or validating admission webhook configuration was created or changed on an AKS or Azure Arc-connected Kubernetes cluster. This may be routine administration, or it may be persistence or credential theft.
en.what_it_detects: Azure Activity Log events whose operationName starts with MICROSOFT.CONTAINERSERVICE/MANAGEDCLUSTERS/ or MICROSOFT.KUBERNETES/CONNECTEDCLUSTERS/ADMISSIONREGISTRATION.K8S.IO and ends with MUTATINGWEBHOOKCONFIGURATIONS/WRITE or VALIDATINGWEBHOOKCONFIGURATIONS/WRITE.
en.why_it_matters: Webhooks see API server requests before they are applied. A mutating webhook can inject a malicious container into every pod for persistence. A validating webhook can record secrets and tokens (T1552.007, container API credentials; T1078).
triage_steps: From the event, note the caller (user, service principal or managed identity), callerIpAddress, the cluster resourceId and the operation status.

Pull the config with kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations or validatingwebhookconfigurations -o yaml. Review clientConfig (external URL or unknown service), rules, namespaceSelector and failurePolicy.
Compare the name and backend with known components such as cert-manager, Gatekeeper/Azure Policy, Kyverno, Istio and Linkerd. Look for a matching Helm release or GitOps deployment.
Check the cluster's kube-audit logs for the Kubernetes identity, the user agent and the exact object change.
For the same caller and cluster within +/- 15 minutes, look for listClusterAdminCredential, role assignments, and new pods, deployments or secrets.
Search for earlier alerts on the same caller or callerIpAddress, and check whether the IP belongs to corporate or CI/CD ranges.
Ask the cluster owner, or check the change ticket, to confirm the change was planned.
false_positives: Administrators deploying or updating admission controllers as planned work.
Helm installs or upgrades of operators like cert-manager, Kyverno or Gatekeeper. cert-manager may rewrite the caBundle periodically.
Azure-managed add-ons (Azure Policy, Istio-based service mesh) or GitOps pipelines (Flux, Argo CD).
response_steps: Confirm with the cluster owner. If the change is legitimate, document it and consider a narrow exclusion by caller and webhook name.
If it is unauthorized, export the webhook YAML as evidence. Then delete or disable the webhook once you confirm the cluster does not depend on it.
Check pods created since the change for injected containers, and remove compromised workloads.
Rotate any secrets, service account tokens and credentials that may have been intercepted. Revoke or disable the caller's credentials.
Review Azure and Kubernetes RBAC, restrict who can write admission webhooks, and watch for the change happening again.
en.severity_rationale: Medium: webhook changes are common in normal administration, but a malicious webhook gives cluster-wide persistence and access to credentials.

positive.description: Unknown user writes a mutating webhook configuration on an AKS managed cluster
Service principal writes a validating webhook configuration on an Azure Arc connected cluster

negative.description: Read of mutating webhook configurations; the suffix is not /WRITE
Write of a different admissionregistration object (ValidatingAdmissionPolicies); the suffix does not match
